messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A collection that must be sorted into categories. their timestamps cannot all be correct even though both contain convincing details. There is not enough information to declare one source simply wrong. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "1. check the timestamps. 2. check the date. 3. check the place. 4. check the name. 5. check the order. 6. one place first. 7. write the date after the name. 8. check the place again. 9. i keep it tidy."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "I count the days. One stamp is missing. I sort the cards by the date. The missing one stays in the pile."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "I put the collection on the board. \"The first one goes here.\" I mark the place with the seed tin. \"The second one says the rain came before the wall.\" I put the third tin beside the fourth. \"The fourth has the date.\" I look at the stamp from the third tin. \"The first one was wrong.\""}, {"id": "R016", "response": "I put the two dates on the same table. One is wrong. I write the wrong date on one corner. Then I check the other corner. The wrong one is in the middle. I sort both into categories. The order is correct now. I keep the wrong one."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "i put the stamp on the step. the date. the hour. i mark the place with the stamp. the category goes under the step. i look at the stamp. i know the day. i put the stamp on the wall. the place stays wrong."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "i mark the first timestamp with a pencil and write the second one on my palm. “the first one is honest, the second is fake.” i add the third one to the sorted list. i know the order matters, so i leave the third one in the pile. i leave the fourth one in my pocket."}, {"id": "R019", "response": "i put the collection on the table and keep both labels on. the first label says 1995, the second says 1996. i put the third label on the shelf because the fourth seems wrong. i move the collection to the table and put the three labels side by side."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "i photograph the timestamps and check whether they match. then i check whether the date is correct. sorry—sorry, i’m putting the date in the same column. sorry—sorry, i’ll leave the category name in place."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "i rub my sore palm and check the timestamps. i ask the source to keep the date in one hand and the category on the other. if the date changes, i mark the old one and keep the new one.if the source is wrong, i mark the date and leave the category alone."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "I mark the oldest timestamp with a strip of paper and tap the shelf twice. I keep the older one until the middle. I put a folded strip of paper beneath it and count each slot twice. I leave the older one beside it. I fold the paper in half and mark the middle with a strip of cloth."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "I mark the first timestamp with pencil and place it beside the second. I tap the third, then the fourth. I read the third once and mark the same place. I put the fourth in the bench and tap the bench once."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "i put the two labels on the bench. the first stamp finds a small crack in the dust. i keep it there and mark the other with a thin line. the collection can stay sorted. i leave the paper folded and leave the label on the bench."}]
